study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative models were estimated using Gaussian process regression (GPR), a Bayesian non-parametric interpolation method that provides both point estimates and predictive confidence measures (uncertainty).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: normative models were estimated using Gaussian process regression (Rasmussen and Williams, 2006), a Bayesian non-parametric interpolation method that yields coherent measures of predictive confidence in addition to point estimates.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) and white matter volume (WMV) segments were used as response variables, estimated from T1-weighted images using voxel-based morphometry (SPM12).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The T1 images served as a basis for the extraction of gray and white matter volumes. ... we estimated normative brain changes across the adult lifespan ... using Gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Wolfers2020.pdf.md: Methods / MRI acquisition; Methods / Normative modeling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as covariates (predictors) to model normative brain structure changes across the lifespan (age 20 to 70 years).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, we used covariates age and sex to predict brain structure at each voxel.
